title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to Grothendieck's 1976 IHES lecture notes on the divided-power de Rham complex. The preceding pages built a double complex C^{**} with an operator T-bar. The de Rham complex DR^{**} sits inside it as Ker T-bar. Its multiplicative and divided-power structures are recovered as extra data, namely 'multiplication' DR^{0,p} x DR^{0,q} -> DR^{0,p+q} and gamma^i: DR^{0,p} -> DR^{0,pi}.

The objects. To make those data explicit, Grothendieck works with graded (or indexed) k-Modules Phi_*, Psi_*, Phi-bar_*. Here 'k-Mod' plausibly means functors on an indexing category with a distinguished object 0. The page uses:
- an extension 0 -> i_{0*}(k) -> Phi-bar_* -> Psi_* -> 0, where i_{0*}(k) is k placed at the index 0;
- Phi_0 = k (implicit) and Psi_0 = 0 (explicit: 'Phi_0 (x) Psi_0 = 0 !!').
Taking exterior powers of this extension gives the standard short exact sequences 0 -> Lambda^{q-1}Psi -> Lambda^q Phi-bar -> Lambda^q Psi -> 0. Tensoring with Gamma^p Phi gives the vertical sequences drawn on the page. The dashed arrows to Lambda^{q+1}Phi_* and Lambda^q Phi_* indicate where these terms are to be mapped: Koszul / de Rham-type terms Gamma^p (x) Lambda^q, as in the PD de Rham complex of a PD polynomial algebra.

The problem. Find a canonical splitting of these sequences for p >= 1.

The NB. Since Gamma^p Phi_* (x) Lambda^q Psi_* is a projective k-Module for p >= 1, some splitting exists. The aim is a simple, canonical choice. The case q = 0 is trivial because Lambda^{-1} = 0.

First case p = q = 1. The sequence is 0 -> Phi_* (x) i_{0*}k -> Phi_* (x) Phi-bar_* -> Phi_* (x) Psi_* -> 0. With the componentwise tensor product and Phi_0 = k, the left term is i_{0*}(k). By the adjunction i_0^* -| i_{0*}:
Hom(Phi (x) Psi, i_{0*}k) = Hom((Phi (x) Psi)_0, k) = Hom(Phi_0 (x) Psi_0, k) = 0.
Any two splittings differ by such a homomorphism, so the splitting is unique, giving Phi (x) Phi-bar = (Phi (x) Psi) (+) i_{0*}k canonically. The page ends by naming the section s: Phi (x) Psi -> Phi (x) Phi-bar to be studied further. Grothendieck writes the target as 'Phi_* (x) Phi_*', probably a slip for Phi_* (x) Phi-bar_*.

Purpose. These splittings would make the 'supplementary data' (multiplication and divided powers on DR) explicit in terms of C^{**}.
errors: The identification under 'Phi_* (x) k' is ambiguous. For the Hom argument to work, Phi_* (x) k must equal i_{0*}(k), which requires a componentwise tensor product with i_{0*}k and Phi_0 = k. Writing it as Phi_* is a slip or ambiguity.
The final line has target 'Phi_* (x) Phi_*'. It should presumably be Phi_* (x) Phi-bar_*, the middle term of the sequence.

The projectivity claim for p >= 1 is asserted without justification; it depends on the unstated hypotheses on Phi_*. The vanishing argument only settles the case p = q = 1; the general p, q case is left open on this page.

ideas.what: Short exact sequences Gamma^p Phi (x) Lambda^{q-1}Psi -> Gamma^p Phi (x) Lambda^q Phi-bar -> Gamma^p Phi (x) Lambda^q Psi coming from an extension of Psi by k, and the search for canonical splittings
ideas.modern_name: Exterior powers of an extension / Koszul filtration; splittings in the PD de Rham (Koszul) complex Gamma^p (x) Lambda^q
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Koszul complexes; divided-power de Rham complex: Berthelot, Illusie)

ideas.what: Uniqueness of the splitting for p = q = 1 by a degree/support argument: Hom(M, i_{0*}k) = Hom(M_0, k), which vanishes because Psi_0 = 0
ideas.modern_name: Adjunction i_0^* -| i_{0*} and a vanishing Hom implying a unique splitting

deep.surprise_reason: Routine technical step: a canonical splitting of exact sequences of exterior powers, with a trivial first case. It serves the unpublished 1976 PD de Rham construction, but the page itself contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: Under 'Phi_* (x) k' the identification is with i_{0*}(k) (written beneath the Hom), not simply Phi_*. The page writes Phi_* (x) k with '‖' and Phi_* below, and i_{0*}(k) appears under the Hom target.
The middle term of the vertical sequence is Gamma^p Phi_* (x) Lambda^q Phi-bar_*; the superscript q is missing in the transcription.
In the Hom line the subscript 'Hom_{k-Mod}' (also read 'k-mod' in the transcription) is consistent; the '!!' emphasises Phi_0 (x) Psi_0 = 0.
